lines.text: The Company had arrived to conduct business. Unfortunately for the local rulers, it had developed an increasingly generous interpretation of the word.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: “The Company believes this matter concluded. I admire its confidence.”
lines.speaker: Yusuf of Hyderabad

lines.text: “I trust the directors will appreciate that fortune favours the bold. Particularly those bold enough to submit a detailed account of their own achievements.”
lines.speaker: Thomas Avery

history.title: Hyderabad · Governor General Tax
history.report:
Resolve the successful Tax’s £2 payment on the table; do not place it in the Governor General’s own treasury.

Add 1 unrest to Hyderabad (now 1).

lines.text: The Company had expected gratitude, or at least obedience. The inhabitants, demonstrating their usual difficulty with administrative terminology, appeared to have confused both with resentment.
lines.speaker: Chronicler

lines.text: “First they took my kingdom. Now they demand that I contribute to its upkeep.”
lines.speaker: Yusuf of Hyderabad

lines.text: The Tax has been recorded. The payment remains a matter for the physical table.
lines.speaker: Arthur Pembroke
